Segments of Route 17 between 1-280 and the San Tomas Expressway experience peak traffic volumes beyond road design capacity. Interstate 680, which parallels Route 17 and provides a supplementary freeway route in the Fremont area, is now complete and adjoins Interstate 280 in the vicinity of Story Road and Route 101. Interstate 280 supplements Route 101 by providing a less congested alternate route to North County and San Mateo County, except for the segment between the Lawrence Expressway and Route 17, where design capacity is also exceeded during peak traffic periods.
Traffic movement on major arterial and collector streets is assisted by the San Jose Traffic Computer facility. An IBM 1800 computer receives and analyzes traffic signals received from throughout the downtown area. Computer programs permit reporting of estimated stops and delays by land and by intersection to provide day-to-day surveillance and evaluation. A total of 420 induction loop detectors have been installed, one for each land or approach to an intersection in the system. All detectors and traffic signal controllers are connected to the computer by cable. The system incorporates three miles of San Carlos Street and a five-by-eight block area of the City's central business district.
Public Transportation
The Santa Clara County Transit District, formed in 1973 from the acquisition and merger of existing private bus companies, operates and maintains the bus system for the County, including San Jose. While the SCCTD bus routes generally adhere to the heavily populated area with the San Jose core area serving as a focal point, service lines also extend throughout north and south County and connect to the Fremont BART station.
During the first years of the Transit District's operation rider patronage grew quickly as the number of buses and the number of routes grew. Recent transient problems with bus maintenance have contributed to a temporary downturn in ridership. The Transit District is continuing to expand its fleet, extend new routes, and generally improve the quality of public transportation in the County.
Traffic and Circulation
Because of the separate characteristics of the circulation network and traffic problems of each neighborhood, the description of traffic and circulation will be made by CNRA. Each individual section will describe the over-all circulation network of the neighborhood and identify any specific traffic problems.
The Highway Research Board has developed a criteria with which to judge the relative congestion of intersections. This descriptive analysis is known as "level of service" and includes six categories of relative congestion.
